newsitem.title: USA: Money manager favors telecom stocks - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Money manager favors telecom stocks - Barron's.

text.p: Henry de Vismes, an investment manager for Citibank Global Asset Management, believes the outlook for selected non-U.S. growth stocks in 1997 is very promising, especially for some telecommunications shares, Barron's newspaper reported on Sunday.
He backs the stocks because earnings will become the key determinant of stock-price movement since interest rates are about as low as they will get in this economic cycle, he said.

De Vismes, the head of international investments for Citibank Global Asset Management, told the newspaper his favorite stocks included Pilipino Telephone Co, a subsidiary of Philippine Long Distance Telephone.
At the current price level, Pilipino is "selling at 17 times 1997 earnings, which are expected to accelerate to plus-45 percent from plus-30 percent this year," de Vismes said.
Another telecom pick is Telefonica del Peru SA. "Short-term investors are out of the stock, and long-term investors will be rewarded."

Russia's PLD Telekom is seen as posting a small loss or breaking even this year, with possible earnings of $0.30 a share next year. "Come 1998, in his view, really big gains in profits could begin," the newspaper said.

De Vismes also liked Misys Plc, a British supplier of software packages; Amway Japan, a seller of cookware, cosmetics and other items; and Powerscreen International Plc, a British maker of screening and crushing equipment for the construction industry.
